subject: Reserved capacity & pricing mechanics for ACME AI — term options and GPU-cost protection
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity & pricing mechanics for ACME AI — term options and GPU-cost protection

Alex / ACME team,

Thanks again for the productive call today. Attached is our initial sizing and commercial starting point for the reserved capacity component of the ACME enterprise agreement. Key bullets below — please review and tell me which of the three pricing/guardrail options you prefer so we can lock an offer for legal to redline:

- Recommended sizing: 40 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) over a 12-month committed term.
- Baseline committed discount (vs on-demand): 15% (option A).
- Option B (indexation): 12% base discount + quarterly GPU-index pass-through adjustment tied to Redwood GPU index (see sheet).
- Option C (fixed price with protection): 18% fixed discount but with an annual GPU-cost protection cap (we absorb up to +6% YoY; beyond that triggers renegotiation or a capped pass-through).

We know procurement wants predictability — so the tradeoff is between larger upfront discounts vs tighter indexation that shares risk. For transparency, the modeling tab shows three scenarios (stable, +20% GPU cost shock, and sustained +40%). I highlighted the customer out-of-pocket under each.

Ask: please confirm (1) preferred option, (2) whether ACME requires a 6-month pricing review window, and (3) any mandatory legal language for the pass-through/cap mechanics. If OK I’ll route to finance for an approval on the discount floor and instruct legal to prepare a DocuSign term for signature.

Attachments: ACME_reserved_modeling_v1.xlsx, term-sheet-draft.pdf

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity & pricing mechanics for ACME AI — term options and GPU-cost protection

Vanessa,

Appreciate the clear options — helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement and legal: 

1) Can you show an example invoice-level impact if GPU input costs increase by 25% mid-term under each option? Ideally a table that shows the incremental pass-through to ACME vs Redwood absorption.
2) ACME prefers a maximum annual pass-through cap of +10% to avoid sudden budget shocks. Is that compatible with Option B (indexation) if we add a 6-month review right to renegotiate?
3) We also want an early-termination protection if cloud GPU commodity costs rise above 40% for more than two consecutive quarters — would Redwood consider a carve-out that allows us to revisit pricing or decommit portions of capacity?

Attaching our procurement checklist for reference. Please loop in finance and legal on your side.

Best,
Alex Morgan
Head of Procurement, ACME AI
procurement@acme.ai

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity & pricing mechanics for ACME AI — term options and GPU-cost protection

Vanessa — quick internal note on approval routing and a recommended construct to reduce downstream escalations: 

- Approval bands: Sales can sign up to 18% committed discount without finance escalation. Anything >18% or any explicit customer carve-out for termination tied to market index (>30%+ sustained) requires finance/FP&A review (Marissa).
- Suggested contract language: include a quarterly GPU index report and a cap mechanism that limits pass-through to ACME to +12% YoY by default. If the index exceeds +12% YoY, the contract moves to a three-month protected negotiation window (no immediate invoice reprice) — practical compromise between predictability and market realism.
- For ACME's requested early-termination trigger (>40% sustained), recommend we offer an option to decommit up to 25% of capacity with a 60-day notice and an associated break fee (calculated in the modeling sheet). This protects Redwood against immediate stranded-capacity costs.

If ACME insists on lower caps (<10%), we need to ask for an additional underwriting credit or a higher minimum committed term (18–24 months) or reduce the reserved size to 30 GPUs.

Attaching internal pricing signoff checklist so legal/finance have all inputs.

Jonas Weber
Director, Enterprise Sales
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ACME AI Legal <legal@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity & pricing mechanics for ACME AI — term options and GPU-cost protection

Alex — thanks for the detail and checklist. Based on internal signoff boundaries and the modeling, here is a commercially executable path we can offer today: 

- Offer: 40 GPUs, 12-month committed term. Committed discount: 15% (final).
- Protection mechanics: Quarterly GPU index with a default pass-through cap of +12% YoY. Redwood will absorb up to +6% YoY for the first contract year as a goodwill buffer.
- Early-decommit: ACME may decommit up to 20% capacity once per 12-month term with 60 days' notice; decommitment triggers a pro-rated break fee equal to 50% of the remaining committed discount value for that capacity.
- Review cadence: 6-month commercial review (mutual).

This keeps the customer-facing cap tighter than our original midpoint, absorbs a small portion of short-term shocks, and preserves an economic guardrail for Redwood. From an approval standpoint Marissa has agreed to sign off on the 15% discount with the above mechanics; if ACME requests a lower pass-through cap (<10%) or asks to remove the break fee we will need a new pricing escalation and potentially add a term extension.

Next steps: I’ll ask legal to redline the term-sheet and push a DocuSign request to ACME. If you can confirm acceptance of the 15%/12% cap/20% decommitment terms, I’ll send the official link.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
